evaluation.notes: The training sequences are made by GRAPH's scripted generator (four attacker styles over a six-host demo network), not by real attackers. The numbers measure how well the model learned that generator's habits on sequences it never saw, and are NOT a claim about real intrusions. Containment success equals precision@1 (contain the top host) or precision@3 (contain the Top-3) by construction in this replay setting. The numbers come only from held-out sequences, never from the rehearsed golden path. On this six-host network at most three hosts can be reached from any host, so a Top-3 list nearly always contains every candidate: precision@3 is about 1.0 for EVERY method and says nothing. Judge the model by precision@1, by calibration, and by its gap to the baselines, and read that gap against the standard error given with precision@1.

detection.model: LCCDE ensemble (LightGBM + XGBoost + CatBoost), leaders chosen on a validation split
detection.dataset: CICIDS2017 (5% sample from the Western OC2 Lab repository)
detection.split: Stratified random 80/20 split after removing duplicate rows (not ordered by time), seed 0
detection.notes: Attack = any class except BENIGN. 44043 rows after removing 12537 duplicates. Share of each attack type still flagged as an attack when the model was trained WITHOUT it: Bot 0.00, BruteForce 0.06, DoS 0.03, Infiltration 0.00, PortScan 0.04, WebAttack 0.01. This is lab data from a public sample, not live traffic, and it is not comparable with NIDS's live Isolation Forest detector.

chapters.label: Detect
chapters.title: A packet becomes evidence.
chapters.body: Scripted traffic enters the detector. The replay marks the compromised host in plain view.

chapters.label: Reconstruct
chapters.title: The path records what changed.
chapters.body: Read the observed compromise separately from the attempted move. ATT&CK labels describe the scripted events.

chapters.label: Forecast
chapters.title: Three reachable futures, ranked.
chapters.body: The model ranks feasible next hosts from repository transition counts. Each share is derived from those counts.

chapters.label: Act
chapters.title: A proposal is not an action.
chapters.body: Review the predicted target, then confirm the simulated response. No real network is changed.

chapters.label: Re-evaluate
chapters.title: The blocked move resolves as a hit.
chapters.body: The forecast is scored against the observed replay. Held-out evaluations also include misses.

chapters.label: Evidence
chapters.title: Read the numbers with their limits.
chapters.body: These results come from held-out or public sample data. They do not establish live detection or protection quality.

chapters.label: Enter
chapters.title: A closed loop, ready to replay.
chapters.body: Detect, forecast, act, and re-evaluate in one scripted demonstration.

copy.promise: See where the attacker goes next, before they get there.
copy.product: Precog SOC detects an intrusion, reconstructs how it spread, forecasts the next host, and lets an analyst contain it in two confirmed steps. Everything you see is a simulation.
